heading.signedOut: Sign in to connect the CLI

subhead.entry: Enter the code your terminal is showing.
subhead.entryPrefilled: Check this is the code your terminal is showing, then continue.
subhead.confirm: Check all four before you approve — this is the only gate on what it gets.
subhead.denied: Good — that is the right call for a code you didn’t ask for.
subhead.unknown: Check for a typo, or start again.
subhead.signedOut: We’ll bring you straight back to this code.

code.label: Device code
code.helper: Eight characters. Lower case and the dash both work — there are no O, I, 0 or 1 to mistake.
code.helperPrefilled: Filled in from the link your terminal opened.
code.helperTypo: One character off is the usual cause.
code.incomplete: A device code is eight characters.

foot.notYou: Didn’t run <cmd>motir login</cmd> yourself? Close this page — nothing is connected until you approve it.

confirm.notYou: Not you? <link>Sign out</link> and sign in as them.
confirm.workspaceHelp: You belong to {count} — it sees only this one.
confirm.cant: Not: archive or delete work items, members, billing.
confirm.expiresHelp: Revoke it in Tokens to disconnect.
confirm.warning: Approve only if you just ran motir login on {hostname} yourself. If someone sent you this code — a chat, an email, a support ticket — deny it: approving hands THEIR terminal everything above, as you.
confirm.warningUnknownHost: Approve only if you just ran motir login yourself. If someone sent you this code — a chat, an email, a support ticket — deny it: approving hands THEIR terminal everything above, as you.

approved.body: Go back to your terminal — motir login has finished and {hostname} is signed in to {workspace}.
approved.bodyUnknownHost: Go back to your terminal — motir login has finished and it is signed in to {workspace}.
approved.bodyAlready: This code was already approved. Go back to your terminal — <cmd>motir login</cmd> has finished and it is connected.
approved.tokenNote: We created a token called <chip>{label}</chip> in this workspace. It expires in {days} days; revoking it disconnects that terminal.

denied.body: Nothing was connected and no token was created. That terminal will report that the request was denied.
denied.retry: Denied it by mistake? Run <cmd>motir login</cmd> again for a fresh code — this one can’t be reused.

expired.body: <chip>{code}</chip> is no longer valid, and nothing was connected. Run <cmd>motir login</cmd> again to get a new code.
expired.terminalNote: Your terminal has already stopped waiting — it reports the code expired.

unknown.body: Codes are eight characters and expire after {minutes} minutes. Run <cmd>motir login</cmd> again if yours is older than that.

signedOut.body: Only the account you sign in as can approve this — and only that account’s workspaces can be picked.

errors.claimedByOther: This code was opened by a different Motir account. Sign in as that account, or run motir login again for a fresh code.
errors.workspaceForbidden: You are not a member of that workspace, so this terminal can’t be connected to it. Pick another one.
errors.notClaimed: We lost track of that code. Enter it again to carry on.
errors.network: We couldn’t reach Motir. Check your connection and try again.
errors.unexpected: Something went wrong on our side. Try again, or run motir login for a fresh code.

projectAccess.noAccessTitle: You don’t have access to this project
projectAccess.noAccessDescription: This project is private. Ask a project admin to add you, or switch to a project you can access.
projectAccess.readOnlyHint: You have read-only access to this project
projectAccess.readOnlyBoardBanner: Read-only access — you can view this board but can’t move or edit work items.

project_administer.label: Administer project
project_administer.description: Change project settings — members, workflow, boards, fields, components and automation.

project_browse.label: View project
project_browse.description: Open the project and read its work items, boards, backlog and reports.

work_item_edit.label: Edit work items
work_item_edit.description: Create, update, assign and move work items, and transition them on the board.

work_item_archive.label: Archive work items
work_item_archive.description: Archive a work item and restore it later. Affects that item only — its children stay.

work_item_delete.label: Delete work items
work_item_delete.description: Permanently delete a work item and everything beneath it. Cannot be undone.

work_item_triage.label: Triage requests
work_item_triage.description: Accept, decline, promote or snooze an item in Triage.

comment_add.label: Add comments
comment_add.description: Post comments on work items, and edit or delete your own.

comment_moderate.label: Moderate comments
comment_moderate.description: Edit and delete anyone's comments, not only your own.

attachment_create.label: Add attachments
attachment_create.description: Upload files onto work items, and delete the ones you uploaded.

attachment_delete_any.label: Delete any attachment
attachment_delete_any.description: Remove attachments uploaded by anyone, not only your own.

watcher_manage.label: Manage watchers
watcher_manage.description: Add and remove other people from a work item's watcher list. Anyone who can view a work item may watch it themselves.

approval_decide_any.label: Decide any approval
approval_decide_any.description: Approve or request changes on an approval routed to someone else, not only one routed to you.

approval_view_any.label: See every approval
approval_view_any.description: See all of the project's approval records, including other people's. Without it you see the approvals routed to you and the ones you decided.

plan_view_any.label: See every plan
plan_view_any.description: See all of the project's AI plans, including other people's. Without it you see the plans you started and the ones routed to you or decided by you.

run_view_any.label: See every agent run
run_view_any.description: See all of the project's agent runs, including other people's. Without it you see the runs you started.

instance_use.label: Use your own agents
instance_use.description: Create, wake, hibernate and delete your own agents on this project — machines charged per running minute. It never opens anyone else's.

page_view.label: Read pages
page_view.description: Open and read the project's pages.

page_edit.label: Edit pages
page_edit.description: Create pages, rename them and change what they say.

page_delete.label: Delete pages
page_delete.description: Permanently delete an archived page and its archived sub-pages.

public_request_comment.label: Comment on requests
public_request_comment.description: Reply on a public request's thread. Public projects only.

public_request_submit.label: Submit requests
public_request_submit.description: Send a bug report or feature request to the project's Requested features. Public projects only.

public_request_upvote.label: Upvote requests
public_request_upvote.description: Vote on a public request to signal demand for it. Public projects only.

member_manage.label: Manage members
member_manage.description: Add and remove project members, and set their roles.

project_manage_access.label: Change project access
project_manage_access.description: Set whether the project is public, open, limited or private.

board_configure.label: Configure boards
board_configure.description: Change board columns, swimlanes and WIP limits.

sprint_manage.label: Manage sprints
sprint_manage.description: Start and complete Sprints, and rank the backlog.

automation_manage.label: Manage automation rules
automation_manage.description: Create, edit and enable the project’s automation and status-derivation rules.

workflow_manage.label: Manage the workflow
workflow_manage.description: Change the statuses a board column projects, and the transitions between them.

component_manage.label: Manage components
component_manage.description: Create, rename and delete the project’s components.

field_manage.label: Manage custom fields
field_manage.description: Create, edit and remove custom field definitions.

label_manage.label: Manage labels
label_manage.description: Create, rename and delete the project’s labels and tags.

report_view.label: View reports
report_view.description: Open the project’s reports — distribution, workload, resolution time, velocity and the roadmap.

saved_filter_manage.label: Manage saved filters
saved_filter_manage.description: Create, edit, share and subscribe to the project’s saved filters.

saved_filter_manage_any.label: Manage anyone’s saved filters
saved_filter_manage_any.description: See other people’s private filters, edit or delete any shared filter, and hand a shared filter to a new owner.

repository_manage.label: Manage repositories
repository_manage.description: Add, remove, move and take over the project’s repositories.

repository_manage_access.label: Manage code access
repository_manage_access.description: Decide which team members may clone the project’s code.

integration_manage.label: Manage integrations
integration_manage.description: Connect and disconnect third-party services for this project — an error monitor, its stored credential, and which of its projects are bound.

import_run.label: Import work items
import_run.description: Bulk-create work items from Jira, Linear or Plane.

ai_configure.label: Configure AI planning
ai_configure.description: Set the planning cadence and whether explanations are drafted.

ai_plan.label: Run AI planning
ai_plan.description: Submit a planning job that spends the workspace’s AI credits and proposes plan changes.

ai_view_plan.label: Author AI plans
ai_view_plan.description: Add proposals to a generated plan and close it for review. Reading a plan needs only project access.

ai_decide_plan.label: Approve or decline AI plans
ai_decide_plan.description: Turn a plan’s proposals into real work items, or end the plan without creating any.

lesson_view.label: View the lesson library
lesson_view.description: Read what the project's AI planner learned from its own planning work.

lesson_manage.label: Change the lesson library
lesson_manage.description: Retire a lesson or add one — both change the standing instructions the planner is given.

lesson_reinforce.label: Record a lesson recurrence
lesson_reinforce.description: Note that a lesson's mistake happened again. It changes nothing the lesson says.

workItems.TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_KIND: A type and executor can only be set on a task, subtask, or bug — not on an epic or story.
workItems.MISSING_ARTIFACT_EVIDENCE: A "deploy" work item can't be closed until a comment on it records the artifact it published — a version (1.4.0), a registry digest (sha256:…) or an integrity hash (sha512-…). If this deliverable genuinely has no identifier, add a comment beginning "NO ARTIFACT:" with the reason.
workItems.CONTAINER_HAS_OPEN_CHILDREN: This item can't reach that status while children of its own have not been implemented. A parent there claims everything under it is built, and its pull request is opened on that claim. Land the children, re-parent them out if they are no longer in scope, or move the item to Done — which completes them deliberately rather than as a side effect.

workItems.APPROVAL_GATE_PENDING_MERGE: This status can't be set directly — the item has an open pull request, and merging it is what makes this move. Every other move is still open.
workItems.PLAN_TARGET_HELD: Status can't be changed while a plan is open — a plan is rewriting this item. Approve or decline the plan, or withdraw the proposal that names this item.
workItems.OBSOLESCENCE_REQUIRES_FINISHED: Only a finished item can be marked — archive it instead.

buildInPublic.confirmLead: Your project becomes a public page anyone on the web can open — no account needed, and search engines can index it. Here's exactly what changes:
buildInPublic.bulletBoard: Your board and roadmap — status, progress, and what's shipping.
buildInPublic.bulletItems: Your work items — titles, types, and descriptions, crawlable by search engines.
buildInPublic.bulletSignIn: Visitors sign in only to submit a request, upvote, or comment — they can't edit anything.
buildInPublic.bulletPrivate: Stays private: assignees, estimates, and internal comments are never shown.
buildInPublic.reassurance: You can stop building in public anytime — the page goes offline and the public link stops working. Submitted requests and upvotes are kept.
buildInPublic.promoSub: Turn the project into a public build-in-public page.
buildInPublic.promoBullet1: Share your board, roadmap, and work items with anyone — no account needed, indexable by search engines.
buildInPublic.promoBullet2: Let people submit, upvote, and comment on requests — they sign in only to act.
buildInPublic.promoBullet3: Internal fields stay private — assignees, estimates, and internal comments are never shown.
buildInPublic.stopConfirmLead: The project goes back to its previous access. Here's what happens:
buildInPublic.stopBulletOffline: The public page goes offline — visitors and search engines can no longer open it.
buildInPublic.stopBulletLink: The public link stops working until you build in public again.
buildInPublic.stopBulletKept: Submitted requests, upvotes, and comments are kept — nothing is deleted.
buildInPublic.stopReassurance: You can start building in public again anytime from Settings.

public.linkSubheading: Share this project with anyone — no account needed to view.
public.linkNote: Anyone can open this link with no sign-in, and the page is crawlable by search engines. Visitors sign in only to submit, upvote, or comment. To stop sharing, set the access level above to anything other than Building in public.
public.heroOverviewSubheading: The tagline, tags and README visitors see on your public page.
public.heroOverviewNote: Opens Settings › Public page. You can write it before the project is public.

data.title: Data & privacy
data.subtitle: Take a copy of your data, or close your account for good. Both are yours to do here, without asking anyone.

export.title: Export your data
export.subtitle: A copy of everything in your account, in a format you can read and load somewhere else. This is your right of access and your right to portability — one file serves both.

profile.name: Your profile and account
profile.desc: Name, email, avatar, language and appearance preferences, sign-in methods, the sessions and tokens you hold (their names and scopes — never their secrets).

workspaces.name: Your workspaces and projects
workspaces.desc: Every workspace you are a member of, with its projects, work items, comments, sprints, boards and saved filters — as far as your access reaches.

files.name: Your files
files.desc: Attachments and images you uploaded, under their original names, in a files/ folder the JSON points into.

export.format: Format JSON + your files, in one .zip — structured, commonly used and machine-readable, which is what lets one export answer both rights
export.window: Answered within one month, usually within minutes
export.requestDesc: Motir builds the file in the background and emails you when it is ready.

preparing.headline: Preparing — requested {requested}.
preparing.body: We'll email {email} when it's ready — you can close this page.

failed.headline: Something went wrong while building your export.
failed.body: Nothing was sent, and nothing in your account changed. Try again, or write to {mailbox} and a person will build it for you.

expired.headline: This export is no longer available.
expired.body: A built export is kept for {days} days, and this one has passed that. Request it again and Motir will build you a fresh copy.

export.expiry: Each Download makes a fresh, private link that expires after five minutes, so the file cannot be shared by forwarding a URL.
export.retention: Request it again any time — the copy above is kept for {days} days.
export.error: We couldn't start your export. Try again in a moment.

delete.title: Delete your account
delete.subtitle: Closing your account starts a {days}-day countdown. Until it runs out you can sign in and stop it; after that the erasure cannot be undone.
delete.rowDesc: Motir will show you exactly what is deleted, what is anonymised and what it has to keep, before you confirm.

blocked.title: One thing has to be handed over first. Motir will not quietly leave an organization without an owner, and it will not delete one out from under the people in it.
blocked.body: You own an organization that other people belong to. Transfer ownership to one of them and this page unblocks itself — you do not need to ask anyone at Motir.
blocked.orgRow: {count, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} · you are the owner
blocked.disabledReason: Available once you have transferred every organization you own.
blocked.workspaces: Workspaces are not a block. {count, plural, one {You are the only member of one of them, so it cannot be left behind — it is deleted with your account, and the confirmation lists it.} other {You are the only member of # of them, so they cannot be left behind — they are deleted with your account, and the confirmation lists them.}} To keep one, invite somebody to it first.

confirm.title: Delete your Motir account?
confirm.body: Exactly what happens to everything attached to {email}. Some of it belongs to other people; some of it Motir is required to keep.
confirm.helper: Your email address is your account's name — typing it is the last check that this is the account you meant.
confirm.schedule: Nothing is erased today. Your account closes now and is erased on {date}. Signing back in does not cancel it — until then you can stop the erasure from the banner on every page, or here on Data & privacy.
confirm.error: We couldn't schedule the deletion. Try again in a moment.
confirm.blockedError: You still own an organization other people belong to. Transfer it before deleting your account.

identity.name: Your profile and how you sign in
identity.desc: Name, email, avatar, preferences, passkeys, two-factor, tokens.

soleWorkspaces.name: Workspaces where you are the only member
soleWorkspaces.desc: {names}. Nobody else can open {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}, so {count, plural, one {it goes} other {they go}} with you. To keep one, invite somebody to it first.

soleWorkspacesWork.name: The work inside them
soleWorkspacesWork.desc: {projects, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}}, with their attachments and history.

dataExports.name: Data exports you asked for
dataExports.desc: {count, plural, one {The request, and the archive it built} other {Every request, and the archive each one built}} — a copy of everything this account held. A file you have already downloaded is yours to keep.

comments.name: Comments in projects other people share
comments.desc: Your name comes off; the comment stays, because it is part of a conversation others took part in.

workItems.name: Work items you reported or were assigned there
workItems.desc: The item stays with its project; the attribution goes.

billing_records.name: Invoices and tax records
billing_records.desc: For as long as Dutch tax law requires — generally seven years. Erasure does not reach a record we are obliged to hold.

backups.name: Backups, until they rotate
backups.desc: Overwritten on their own schedule, and never restored to active use.

grace.title: Your account will be erased on {date}
grace.body: {daysLeft}. Until then nothing has changed: you are signed in, your workspaces are open, and your team sees no difference. Cancel and the countdown stops — there is no penalty and no second confirmation.
grace.daysLeft: {days, plural, =0 {Less than a day left} one {# day left} other {# days left}}
grace.exportSubtitle: Still available, and worth doing now — after {date} there is nothing left to export.
grace.cancelled: Your deletion is cancelled. Nothing will be erased.
grace.error: We couldn't cancel the deletion. Try again in a moment.

data.mailbox: This pane is not the only route. Anything the product cannot do for you — a correction, a restriction, an objection, or a question about any of it — goes to {mailbox}, which the Privacy Policy publishes and a person answers.

banner.scheduled: Your account is scheduled for deletion on {date}. Everything still works until then.

notifications.defaultsNote: Direct events — mentions, comments on your items, and assignments — default on for both channels. An untouched row uses that default (it is not off until you turn it off).

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.subtitle: Add a second step to your sign-in, so a stolen password is not enough on its own. Motir asks for it after your password, on every new device.

off.title: Two-factor authentication is off
off.body: Turn it on and Motir will ask for a one-time code after your password. Start with an authenticator app — it works offline and is the strongest of the three.

methods.title: Your second factor
methods.subtitle: Motir asks for the primary method first and offers the others as fallbacks.
methods.subtitleOff: Every method Motir offers, and what each one costs you.

totp.name: Authenticator app
totp.desc: A six-digit code from 1Password, Google Authenticator, Authy or any RFC 6238 app. Works with no signal and no inbox.
totp.descOn: Asked for first at every sign-in.

email.name: Email
email.desc: A code sent to {email}. Convenient, but an inbox is not a strong second factor — available once an authenticator is set up.
email.descOn: A code to {email}, valid for {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. Offered at the challenge as “Email me a code” — never asked for first.

backup.name: Recovery codes
backup.desc: Ten single-use codes for the day your phone is gone. Motir generates them the moment you turn 2FA on.

recovery.title: Recovery codes
recovery.subtitle: Single-use codes for the day your authenticator is gone. Each one works once.
recovery.generateDesc: Replaces all ten. The codes you have now stop working the moment the new set is shown.
recovery.low: You have {remaining, plural, one {# recovery code} other {# recovery codes}} left. Generate a new set before you run out.
recovery.exhausted: You’ve used every recovery code. If you lose your authenticator now, only an emailed code can get you back in. Generate a new set.

stepUp.title: Confirm it's you
stepUp.subtitle: Enter your password to change your two-factor settings.
stepUp.noPassword: You sign in with Google, so there’s no password to confirm. Your Google account is what protects this change.

enrol.scanSubtitle: Scan this with 1Password, Google Authenticator, Authy — any app that supports time-based codes.
enrol.cantScanHelp: Type this key into your app instead.
enrol.codeSubtitle: Enter the six digits your app is showing now. It changes every {seconds} seconds.
enrol.codesNext: We’ll show you ten recovery codes next. Keep them — they are how you get back in if you lose the app.

codes.title: Save your recovery codes
codes.subtitle: Ten codes, each usable once. Store them somewhere you can reach without this device.
codes.warning: This is the only time we can show them. Motir stores them encrypted, so we can’t display them again — you can generate a new set, which replaces these.
codes.acknowledge: I’ve saved these codes somewhere safe.

regenerate.title: Generate new recovery codes?
regenerate.body: Your current {remaining, plural, one {# code} other {# codes}} stop working immediately. You’ll get ten new ones, shown once.
regenerate.warning: If you’ve printed the old codes or saved them in a password manager, replace them — they will not work after this.

aiPlanning.title: AI planning
aiPlanning.pageDescription: How Motir's planner keeps this project moving — when it expands the plan, how it packs sprints, and what it writes for each item.

empty.description: Create a project to configure its AI planning settings.

autoPlan.title: Auto-plan
autoPlan.subtitle: Expand the plan automatically when ready work runs low.
autoPlan.enableHint: When ready work drains, Motir drafts the next slice of the plan for you to review.
autoPlan.thresholdHint: Motir starts drafting when fewer than this many work items are ready to start.
autoPlan.pauseConditions: Auto-planning pauses while Motir cannot read your code — when no repository is connected, or the code index is out of date. It also waits while a proposed plan is still undecided, while ready work is above your threshold, when there is nothing left to expand, and while your plan does not include AI planning. Your setting is unchanged, and it resumes on its own once the condition clears.
autoPlan.guardrail: Auto-plan proposes an expansion for your approval — it never creates work without you.

paused.lead: Auto-plan is paused — a plan is waiting for your review.
paused.body: Motir drafts one plan at a time. It picks up again as soon as you approve or decline this one.
paused.staleBody: Your project has changed since this plan was drafted — {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} may be out of date.

sprint.title: AI sprint planning
sprint.subtitle: Pack ready work into short sprints that respect what blocks what.
sprint.enableHint: Motir proposes the next sprints from ready work; you approve before any sprint is created.
sprint.lengthHint: Sized for agent throughput, not human sprints. Widen it if your team works at human pace.
sprint.lengthInvalid: Choose a sprint length between 1 and 14 days.
sprint.rationale: An agent finishes a work item in minutes, so a two-week sprint hides a whole plan inside one bucket. Short sprints keep plan → build → review a loop you can actually watch.

planner.title: Planner
planner.subtitle: How the planner writes for this project.
planner.explanationsLabel: Draft a why for each item
planner.explanationsHint: Every proposed work item gets a short “why this matters” you can read without opening the code.
planner.dataPracticeCommitment: Neither Motir nor its gateway trains on this project's content.
planner.dataPracticeReport: What a provider does with a request once it reaches them is that provider's own published position.

lessonCapture.title: Planning mistakes
lessonCapture.subtitle: What Motir does when a plan it drafted turns out to be wrong.
lessonCapture.enableHint: When a plan turns out to be wrong, Motir writes down the correction and applies it to every plan it drafts for this project afterwards.
lessonCapture.explanation: What gets written down is the correction itself — not your work items and not your code. It stays with this project and is never shared with any other. Motir reads the relevant ones back as it drafts later plans here, so the same mistake is less likely twice. Turn this off and Motir stops writing new ones down; everything it has already learned keeps applying until you stop it.

footer.invalidHint: Fix the highlighted fields to save

aiPlanning.notConnectedBody: AI planning runs on Motir's cloud service. These settings are saved but stay inactive until this deployment is connected to Motir AI.

lessons.cardSubtitle: Corrections this project taught its planner. Motir applies them to every plan it drafts here.
lessons.pageDescription: Corrections this project taught its planner, most recently relevant first. Motir applies each of these to every plan it drafts here — until you stop it.
lessons.applyingBody: It goes into every plan drafted for this project.
lessons.emptyTitle: Motir hasn't learned anything here yet
lessons.emptyBody: When a plan turns out to be wrong — a missing dependency, a work item sized past what one run can finish — Motir writes down the correction and applies it to every plan it drafts for this project afterwards. Those corrections appear here, with what happened and why, so you can read them and decide which ones to keep.
lessons.emptyRecording: Nothing is recorded until a plan is actually corrected. Recording can be switched off in AI planning settings.

effects.title: What readers get
effects.page: Work item pages and quick views show every field in the reader's language: the title, description, explanation and each to-do.
effects.lists: Lists, boards, the backlog, sprints, the roadmap, ready and triage show titles in the reader's language, with a Show original switch on each view.
effects.original: Agents, the API and emails always receive the original text, and editing always opens the original.

translation.cost: Each field is translated once per language and kept, so a later reader of the same text pays nothing, and text already in the reader's language is never sent. Translation spends your organization's AI credits at the model's cost plus 50%. <link>Usage & cost</link>

section.details: Project details, and the acts that change them — the name, the key, the avatar, archiving — are managed by project admins. Ask an admin if something here needs to change.
section.repositories: Where this project's code lives, and who takes it over, is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if a repository needs connecting or moving.
section.members: Who is on this project, and what each of them can do, is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if you need someone added or a role changed.
section.public-page: What this project shows on its public page — its tagline, tags and README — is written by project admins. Ask an admin if something there needs changing.
section.public-address: You need permission to manage this project’s access to open its public address.
section.roles: What each role in this project can do is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if a role needs changing.
section.code-access: Who on this team can clone and push this project's code is managed by project admins. You can still connect your own GitHub account from Git settings.
section.workflow: Statuses and the transitions between them are managed by project admins. Ask an admin if the workflow needs changing.
section.approvals: Which approvals this project asks for — and the gates that hold work until somebody presses them — is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if a gate needs turning on or off.
section.board: Board configuration — columns, limits and swimlanes — is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if a column or a limit needs changing.
section.estimation: How this project estimates work is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if the scale needs changing.
section.fields: Custom fields are managed by project admins. Ask an admin if a field needs adding or changing.
section.components: Components are managed by project admins. Ask an admin if one needs adding or changing.
section.bugs: Where this project's bugs are filed is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if the destination needs changing.
section.ai-planning: AI planning for this project — its cadence — is configured by project admins. Ask an admin if it needs changing.
section.hosted-agent: Which model a hosted run uses is shown to people who can start a hosted run on this project. Ask a project admin if you need to see it.
section.translation: Whether this project's work content is translated for each reader is shown to people who can read the project's work items. Ask a project admin if you need to see it.
section.automation: Project automation is managed by project admins. Ask an admin if you need a rule changed.
section.monitoring: This project's error-monitor connection is managed by people who can manage integrations. Ask a project admin if Sentry needs connecting or reconnecting.

burndown.what: How the sprint's scope, completed and started work move from its start to its end, with a target line and a Today marker.
burndown.how: Completed rising toward Scope means the sprint is on track. A Scope line that climbs after the start is scope creep; a Completed line that lags the Target is behind.

velocity.what: The story points a team committed to against the points it completed, sprint by sprint.
velocity.how: Compare the two bars in each sprint. Steady completed bars show a reliable pace you can plan the next sprint against; pick an earlier sprint to look back from there.

sprintReport.what: A finished or running sprint on one page: what was completed, what was not, what was added after it started, and its sprint graph.
sprintReport.how: Start with completed against not completed, then read the work added mid-sprint. Use the picker under the title to switch sprint.

createdVsResolved.what: How many work items were created and how many were resolved in each period.
createdVsResolved.how: When the created bar is taller than the resolved bar the backlog is growing; when it is shorter the team is catching up. Use the series switches to look at one of them alone.

distribution.what: How the project's work items split across the values of one field, such as status, type or assignee.
distribution.how: The wider a slice, the more work items carry that value. Change the statistic to cut the same work another way.

averageAge.what: The average number of days the unresolved work items had been open at the end of each period.
averageAge.how: A line that keeps rising means work is being left open. Compare it with the window average to see whether the latest period is unusual.

resolutionTime.what: The average number of days it took to resolve the work items resolved in each period.
resolutionTime.how: A falling line means work is being finished faster. Periods are counted by resolution date, so an old item resolved today raises today's period.

workload.what: The open work each person holds over a chosen period, counted in story points or work items. Work with no assignee is counted under its reporter.
workload.how: The longest bars are the people carrying the most open work. Look for a very uneven spread before assigning more.

publicProjects.faqA1: Yes. This is a public project — anyone on the web can view it with no account, and it’s indexable by search engines. You only need to sign in to submit, upvote, or comment on requests.
publicProjects.faqQ2: How do I submit a request?
publicProjects.faqA2: Use the “Submit a request” button. You’ll be asked to sign in first (sign-in-to-act), then your bug or idea lands in the team’s Requested features and can appear on the public roadmap.
publicProjects.faqQ3: What’s hidden on the public view?
publicProjects.faqA3: Internal fields are stripped by the public projection: assignees, estimates, story points, and internal work-item comments are never sent to the public view — they’re absent from the data, not just hidden in the page.

projectSquare.heroLede: Browse real, public product roadmaps and project plans from teams building in the open — issues, boards, and sprints, free to read with no sign-up. Search by name, filter by topic, and sort by what's trending.

projectSquare.faqLede: The project square is a public, crawlable directory of every project teams have chosen to build in the open on Motir — their real roadmaps, boards, and sprints, free to read with no account.
projectSquare.faqA1: It's a public directory of project plans built on Motir. Every listed project is public by choice — you can read its roadmap, board, and work items with no sign-up.
projectSquare.faqQ2: Are these projects free to view?
projectSquare.faqA2: Yes. Every project in the square is fully public and free to read — no account, no paywall. You only need an account to create your own project.
projectSquare.faqA3: Trending surfaces projects with recent upvotes and activity, Popular ranks by lifetime upvotes, and New lists the most recently published — each a shareable, crawlable URL.
projectSquare.footerTagline: The AI-native way to plan, track, and ship — explore what teams are building in the open.

ci.drawingTitle: You're past your included minutes — CI is now drawing credits.
ci.drawingBody: {over} minutes over · {credits} credits drawn this period, at 1 credit per minute. Nothing is blocked.
ci.zeroTitle: All of this project's repositories are your own,
ci.zeroBody: so GitHub bills you for Actions directly and Motir isn't paying for any CI. Your {pool} included minutes are there if you ever ask Motir to host a repository.
ci.pausedTitle: CI is paused — your credits ran out.
ci.pausedBody: You used all {pool} included minutes and the {over} minutes since then drew {credits} credits, which emptied your Motir AI balance. Until this is resolved, no workflows run on the repositories Motir hosts for you, and new work can't be dispatched. Nothing has been deleted, and your code is untouched.
ci.pausedTitleMember: CI is paused — this organization is out of credits.
ci.pausedBodyMember: Workflows won't run on the repositories Motir hosts, and new work can't be dispatched, until an organization owner or admin adds credits or moves the repositories to your own GitHub. Nothing has been deleted, and your code is untouched.
ci.memberLockNote: Billing for this organization is managed by its owner and admins. There is no action for you here — this line is informational.
ci.balanceUnavailable: Your credit balance is temporarily unavailable. Your minutes are accurate and nothing is paused — only the balance figure is missing.
ci.optionCreditsBody: Top up your Motir AI balance. CI keeps running on Motir's repositories and the overage keeps drawing 1 credit per minute.
ci.optionCreditsCost: CI resumes within a minute of the payment landing — at most 15.
ci.optionMoveTitle: Move the repositories to your own GitHub
ci.optionMoveBody: GitHub bills you for Actions directly from then on, and Motir stops charging CI credits. The code is yours either way — this changes who pays for the compute.
ci.optionMoveCost: Needs a GitHub account you own, a transfer you accept on GitHub (it isn't instant), and re-installing the Motir app so dispatch keeps working.

agents.rate: Machine time is 1 credit per running minute. Storage is 10 credits per agent per day, asleep or not. Both draw from your Motir AI balance.
agents.zero: No agents ran or existed this month. Machine time is 1 credit per running minute. Storage is 10 credits per agent per day, asleep or not.

search.overdraftTitle: Search keeps working when your balance runs out.

search.unavailable: Search figures aren’t available right now. Your searches are still being charged — this is the display, not the billing.

inputs.runCategoriesHelp: Pick one to three. The run is split evenly across what you pick: one takes 100%, two take 50% each, all three take 33% each. You never choose a model — each category lists the models it serves as examples.

landing.headline: What do you want to build?
landing.subhead: Describe your idea. Motir plans the whole project — brand, pricing, marketing and the code — tracks every kind of work, and ships the code for you.

say.title: Say what you want

watch.title: Watch it take shape

decide.title: You decide
decide.body: Every piece comes back to you to look at, try and approve. You stay in charge of what ships.

developers.title: How Motir works, for developers
developers.body: Every Motir project runs through the same instrument: the modules are Motir and its agents, and the switches are yours. motir.co walks through it module by module.

fix.lead: Hand the repair to an agent from your terminal:
fix.how: An agent works on the pull request's own branch, pushes, and the checks run again.
fix.howMany: An agent works on each pull request's own branch, pushes, and the checks run again.

fixing.why: Only one fix runs at a time. The checks run again when the agent pushes.

child.pointer: Run the fix from <link>{key}</link> — this work item was built as part of that run, so its repair runs there.

which.failed: A queue failure needs new commits, even a flaky one. motir fix hands it to an agent, which merges the base branch first and pushes. Approving again is not offered: it would queue the same commits the queue just refused.

fix.conflictOn: <prs></prs> conflicts with {base} and cannot be merged.

fix.rearm: There is nothing to approve here. A push moves the head, which re-arms the question, and the next green raises the merge gate once — over the new commits.
fix.sentBackByAgent: The review agent sent these commits back. An agent fixes them on {count, plural, one {the same pull request} other {the same pull requests}}, with its findings in the prompt.

connect.title: Connect GitLab
connect.subtitle: One authorization on GitLab covers your identity and project access.

step1.title: Connect your GitLab account
step1.body: Authorize Motir on GitLab in one step. This confirms who you are and grants API access to the projects you're a member of — Motir reads merge requests and pipelines and adds webhooks only on the projects you connect next. One grant covers identity and access — there's no separate app to install.

step2.title: Choose projects in Motir
step2.body: After you authorize, pick which of your GitLab projects to sync — right here in Motir, not on a separate screen. Motir only touches the projects you connect, and you can disconnect any of them any time.

connect.foot: You'll be sent to GitLab to authorize, then choose projects here.

projects.title: Projects
projects.caption: The GitLab projects Motir syncs. Connecting a project lets Motir read its merge requests and pipelines.
projects.empty: No projects connected yet. Connect a project to start syncing merge requests and pipelines.
projects.foot: Connecting a project adds a webhook for merge-request, pipeline, push and deployment events. Motir does not build a code index for GitLab projects, so AI planning cannot read their source.
projects.noProjects: No projects to connect — every project you're a member of is already connected.
projects.memberOnly: Only projects you're a member of on GitLab appear here — Motir can't see any others.

error.not_connected: GitLab isn't connected. Reconnect to choose projects.
error.not_found: That project isn't among your GitLab memberships anymore.
error.unavailable: Couldn't reach GitLab — your authorization may have been revoked. Reconnect GitLab and try again.
error.webhook_not_configured: This Motir server has no GitLab webhook secret configured, so it can't receive project events. Ask whoever runs it to set GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
error.webhook_failed: Couldn't add Motir's webhook to that project. Adding a webhook needs the Maintainer role on the project in GitLab.
error.organization_closing: This organization is scheduled for deletion, so no project can be connected.

connect.preflightRepositories: Choose all repositories, or only the ones you select. You can change this later on GitHub.
connect.preflightAccess: Approve the access the App asks for. It can read and change code and pull requests, and read checks, deployments, issues, merge queues, metadata and security events.
connect.preflightReturn: GitHub sends you straight back to this step, and it shows the repositories you connected.
connect.ownerPendingTitle: Waiting for an owner to approve

index.heading: Indexing your codebase
index.body: Motir builds one code graph for the project across all your repositories — files, symbols and how they reference each other. This can take a few minutes for a large codebase.
index.waiting: Waiting for repositories to be indexed…
index.callout: Motir derives your conventions + a code-health check (and any plan) from the whole project, so it needs every repo indexed — Next stays disabled until every repository finishes.
index.completeNote: Per-repo conventions + a code-health check derived from your code — nothing to approve (they live on the Code health page). You're set up.

import.heading: Bring in your existing backlog
import.body: Import from Jira, Linear or Plane, or enter Motir and do it later. An import keeps going in the background.
import.reconcile: When you then generate a plan, Motir reconciles the two so nothing is duplicated.
import.bodyInline: Already tracking work in Jira, Linear, GitHub, Plane or a CSV? Bring it in right here. You review a dry-run preview before anything is written. Skip this if you have no backlog to bring in.
import.running: Importing from {source} · {done} work items so far
import.runningBody: This keeps going in the background. You don't have to wait for it.

decision.heading: Your codebase is in Motir
decision.body: Motir can plan what's next now, or you can finish and plan later from the project. You decide what ships.

resume.heading: Continue planning
resume.body: You started planning this project. Continue in the planning workspace.

questions.body: Motir has read your code. A few answers about where the project is going, and it drafts your first plan from both.
questions.draftingBody: From your code, your backlog and your answers. You can leave this page; Motir tells you when it is ready.

repositorySet.identityCaption: This is the account Motir invited

repositorySet.actionError: That didn't work. Nothing was changed — try again.

repositoryTakeover.title: Repositories
repositoryTakeover.lead: Only the repositories {projectName} works on — whether Motir hosts them or {org} does.
repositoryTakeover.hostedHint: Motir created these and pays for their CI. Move any of them to your own GitHub whenever you want.
repositoryTakeover.empty: No repositories in this project yet. Add one {org} already has, or connect a new repository.
repositoryTakeover.pausedTitle: CI is paused — this organization is out of credits.
repositoryTakeover.pausedBody: Moving a repository to your own GitHub turns its Actions back on and GitHub bills you for them from then on.
repositoryTakeover.pausedOtherProjects: Motir also hosts repositories for {projects} — moving this project's does not move theirs.
repositoryTakeover.yoursDetail: You already own this one — nothing to move, and Motir never bills its CI.
repositoryTakeover.statePending: Waiting for you to accept on GitHub
repositoryTakeover.statePendingStale: Still waiting for you to accept on GitHub
repositoryTakeover.pendingDetail: GitHub sent the transfer to {login}. It stays here until you accept it there — nothing expires on Motir's side, and the repository keeps working in the meantime.
repositoryTakeover.pendingDetailStale: Sent to {login} on {date} and not accepted yet. Nothing is wrong and nothing was lost — the repository is still here and still working. Accept it on GitHub to finish, or just leave it.
repositoryTakeover.reinstallDetail: The repository is yours — the transfer went through. Install the Motir app on {login} and tick {repo} when GitHub asks which repositories it may see.
repositoryTakeover.reinstallDetailStale: It's yours and it stays yours. Motir just can't reach it to dispatch work until the app is installed on {login} with this repository selected.
repositoryTakeover.reinstallConsequence: Until you do, Motir can't dispatch work to this repository — your plan and your history are untouched.
repositoryTakeover.doneDetail: Moved to {login} on {date}. GitHub bills you for Actions on it from now on, and Motir no longer charges CI credits for it. Dispatch is working.
repositoryTakeover.failedOrgPermission: GitHub declined the transfer to {owner} — you need permission to create repositories in that organization. The repository is still here and still works; nothing was changed.
repositoryTakeover.actionError: That didn't go through. Nothing was changed — try again.
repositoryTakeover.modalLead: Motir transfers this repository out of its organization and into yours. Your work items, history and dispatch stay exactly where they are.
repositoryTakeover.orgsLoadingHint: You can go ahead with your personal account — the lookup only adds organizations.
repositoryTakeover.orgsFailed: Motir couldn't reach your GitHub organizations just now, so only your personal account is listed.
repositoryTakeover.orgPermissionNote: Moving into an organization needs permission to create repositories there — GitHub refuses the transfer otherwise, and Motir says so rather than silently hiding the option.
repositoryTakeover.costAccountDetail: It goes to {login}, the account you connected.
repositoryTakeover.costTransfer: A transfer you accept on GitHub. It isn't instant.
repositoryTakeover.costTransferDetail: GitHub asks {login} to accept it. Nothing moves until you do, and nothing expires on Motir's side while you take your time.
repositoryTakeover.costReinstall: Re-installing the Motir app on the new owner.
repositoryTakeover.costReinstallDetail: An app installation belongs to an account, so it does not travel with the repository. Until you re-install, Motir can't dispatch work to it.
repositoryTakeover.billingConsequence: GitHub bills you for Actions directly from then on, and Motir stops charging CI credits.
repositoryTakeover.billingConsequenceDetail: The code is yours either way — this changes who pays for the compute. Actions come back on for this repository as part of the move, even while your organization is out of credits.
repositoryTakeover.connectWhy: Motir needs one thing to move a repository to you: the GitHub account it belongs to. It is the same account it invites you to your code with — you'll see which one.

apiDocs.mcpLede: Motir's project plan is reachable by any Model Context Protocol client over one endpoint. Point your agent at it with a personal access token and it can read the ready set, claim the next item, create work, move statuses and comment — through the same services, permissions and data the web app uses.
apiDocs.mcpForkHeading: Should you use this, or the REST API?
apiDocs.mcpForkIntro: Motir publishes two programmatic surfaces over the same domain. They are not alternatives with the same trade-off, and the difference is worth thirty seconds before you pick.
apiDocs.mcpStepTokenBody: In the app: **Settings → Account → Tokens → Create**. Give it a label and an expiry. The plaintext is shown **once** — copy it then; Motir keeps only a hash.
apiDocs.mcpStepWire: Point your client at the endpoint
apiDocs.mcpStepWireBody: Every client needs the same four facts. They are Motir’s, they are the same for every agent, and everything below this table is one of them transcribed into a vendor’s file format.
apiDocs.mcpSecretCallout: Don’t paste the token into a file your repository tracks. Where your client can read it from somewhere else, the block below does that instead.
apiDocs.mcpStepCheckBody: Call `whoami`. It takes no arguments and answers with the user the token belongs to, the workspace it is bound to, and the scopes it was granted — so one call confirms all three at once.
apiDocs.mcpUnauthorized: A **401** means the token is absent, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired — the five are deliberately not distinguished, so a caller cannot probe token state. Mint a fresh one and try again.
apiDocs.mcpToolsLede: Every tool the Motir MCP server exposes, and the scope that gates it. Grouped by scope, because that is the choice you make when you mint the token — leave a scope off and its whole group refuses.
apiDocs.mcpToolsMeta: {tools} tools · {permissions} permissions · derived from the server’s own permission map
apiDocs.mcpToolsSummaryNote: These are the summaries. For a tool’s exact arguments and response shape, see the reference — it is kept beside the code because those facts change most.
apiDocs.mcpToolsEmptyBody: This page builds its list from the server’s own scope map. If that read fails the page says so rather than showing an empty column — the rail, the wiring guide and every other address still work.

next.overturned: Nothing resumes. The approval no longer stands, so the run waits for a new decision on {key}.
next.reshaped: Resume will carry the re-shaped story.

imp.body: Opens {org}’s app as {email} in a staff session. A banner stays on every page until you exit or the session expires.
imp.lengthHint: At most 60 minutes. A new session needs a new reason.
imp.readOnlyNote: Read-only: you see exactly what {firstName} sees, and every control that would change something is disabled.
imp.fullWarning: Full access acts as {firstName}. Anything you change is real and lands in {org}’s data, recorded as made by you on {firstName}’s behalf.
imp.reasonLabel: Reason — required, written to the audit log
imp.reasonHint: Recorded on the session and on every action taken in it.
imp.failedTitle: The staff session did not start

ineligible.self: You can’t view Motir as yourself.
ineligible.platform_staff: This account is platform staff. Staff never view as staff.
ineligible.suspended_account: This account is suspended, so there is nothing to see as it.
ineligible.suspended_organization: This account’s organization is suspended. Reactivate it first, or review it from the console.
ineligible.no_workspace: This account belongs to no workspace, so there is no app to open.

error.REASON_REQUIRED: A reason is required — it is recorded on the session and on every action taken in it.
error.NOT_FOUND: That account no longer exists. Reload the page.
error.INELIGIBLE: This account can’t be viewed as right now. Reload the page to see why.
error.INVALID: Pick an access level and a length the console offers.
error.NOT_PERMITTED: Only a superadmin can start a staff session.
error.FAILED: Something went wrong and no session was started. The failure has been logged.

bar.full: Acting as {name} ({email}) · {org} — staff session, full access, every change is yours, ends at {time}

ended.title: Your staff session ended at {time}
ended.body: You are no longer viewing Motir as {name}. The session and everything you opened in it are in the audit log.

endedBy.revoked: It stopped being valid before its time ran out — you signed out, your platform role changed, or the account was suspended.

status.title: Organization status
status.subtitle: Suspending an organization refuses every member of every workspace under it.
status.active: {members, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} across {workspaces, plural, one {# workspace} other {# workspaces}} can sign in and work.
status.suspendedEffect: Every member is refused at their next request. Nothing has been deleted.

suspend.title: Suspend {org}?
suspend.lead: Suspension is the lever for non-payment or abuse. From the moment you confirm:
suspend.c1: All {members} members of all {workspaces} workspaces are refused at their next request and see that the organization is suspended.
suspend.c2: New planning jobs and agent runs are refused; running ones are stopped.
suspend.c3: Nothing is deleted. Work items, repositories and the ledger stay exactly as they are, and another superadmin can reactivate it.

reactivate.title: Reactivate {org}?
reactivate.body: All {members} members can sign in and work again from their next request. Kill-switches keep their own state — a switch you turned off stays off.

reason.label: Reason — required, written to the audit log
reason.placeholder: Why are you doing this? Name the ticket if there is one.
reason.hint: Shown to any operator reading this organization later. “Support” on its own answers nothing.

result.suspended: Suspended {org}. Its members are refused from their next request.
result.reactivated: Reactivated {org}. Its members can work again.
result.granted: Granted {n} credits to {org}. The ledger and the audit log both carry it.
result.adjusted: Adjusted {org}’s balance by {n} credits. The ledger and the audit log both carry it.
result.planUnchanged: {org} was already on {tier}. The assignment is recorded.
result.replayed: That action had already landed — nothing new was written.
result.creditUnreachable: Couldn’t reach the credit service. Nothing was granted and nothing was recorded. Try again in a moment.

error.REASON_REQUIRED: A reason is required — it is written to the audit log.
error.NOT_FOUND: This organization no longer exists. Reload the page.
error.ALREADY_IN_STATE: Someone else changed this first. Reload the page to see where it stands.
error.NOT_PERMITTED: Only a superadmin can do this.
error.FAILED: Something went wrong and nothing was changed. The failure has been logged.
error.AMOUNT_INVALID: Enter a whole number of credits the ledger can hold.
error.LARGE_GRANT_UNCONFIRMED: A grant this large needs the organization’s slug typed to confirm.
error.INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: That would take the balance below zero.
error.CONFLICT: The credit service refused it as a conflict with an earlier action. Reload and try again.
error.REJECTED: The credit service refused it. Check the amount or the plan and try again.
error.CREDIT_SERVICE_UNREACHABLE: Couldn’t reach the credit service. Nothing was granted and nothing was recorded. Try again in a moment.
error.UNKNOWN_KEY: That switch no longer exists. Reload the page.

credits.title: Credits & plan
credits.subtitle: Credits are Motir’s internal unit, never a currency. Read from the credit service; every write is recorded.

error.title: Couldn’t load credits
error.body: The credit service didn’t answer, so the balance, plan and ledger aren’t shown. Nothing is zero — the figures simply aren’t loaded. Status and kill-switches above still work.

grant.title: Grant credits to {org}
grant.body: Adds credits to the org’s balance as a grant row in its ledger. It changes no plan and touches no Stripe object.
grant.large: This is a large grant — {threshold} credits or more. Type the org’s slug to confirm.

adjust.title: Adjust {org}’s balance
adjust.body: Corrects the balance with an adjustment row — for a billing mistake. A goodwill credit is a grant, not an adjustment.
adjust.hint: Use − to remove credits. The balance may not go below zero.

plan.title: Change {org}’s AI plan
plan.body: Sets the tier the org’s credit allotment is read from.
plan.stripe: {org} pays for its plan through Stripe. This changes the tier Motir reads; it does not change or cancel the Stripe subscription, and the subscription’s next event sets the tier from Stripe again.

empty.title: No credit transactions yet
empty.body: {org} has not been charged, topped up or granted anything. Its balance is 0 credits.

switches.title: Kill-switches
switches.subtitle: Durable per-organization switches, ON by default. A change takes effect on the org’s next request — no deploy.
switches.suspendedNote: This organization is suspended, so every switch evaluates OFF whatever is set here.
switches.unavailable: The kill-switches couldn’t be loaded. Reload the page to try again.

confirmOn.title: Turn {switch} back on for {org}?
confirmOn.body: {switch} works again for every member of {org} from their next request.

ai_planning.name: AI planning
ai_planning.whenOff: New planning jobs are refused with “planning is paused for your organization”. Jobs already running finish.

hosted_runs.name: Hosted agent runs
hosted_runs.whenOff: New agent runs and agent instances are refused. Running containers are stopped.

web_search.name: Web search
web_search.whenOff: Planning and agents run without web search; a search call returns “not available”.

ops.readOnlyRole: Only a superadmin can change these. You can see them with the {role} role.

audit.title: Platform actions on this organization
audit.subtitle: Every operator write on this org, newest first. Append-only.
audit.empty: No operator has changed anything on this organization yet.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: Every platform-staff action, newest first. Append-only and hash-chained: an entry changed after it was written breaks the chain from that entry on.

chain.okDetail: All {count} entries hash-chain intact, checked through #{last} at {time}.
chain.broken: The chain is broken at entry #{n} ({at}). That entry no longer matches the hash recorded for it, so it and the {after} entries after it can’t be trusted as written. This check changed nothing; the entries are shown as stored.
chain.label: Chain integrity

filter.label: Filter the audit log
filter.tenantPlaceholder: Any organization — paste an org id
filter.invalid: Those filters can’t be read. Check the dates and clear the page position.

detail.genesis: the first entry — chained to nothing

empty.title: No entries match these filters
empty.body: Nothing was recorded that matches. Widen the dates, or switch to Writes & reads.

suspended.title: {org} is suspended
suspended.body: Your organization’s access to Motir is paused. Nothing has been deleted. Contact your organization’s owner, or write to support@motir.co.
suspended.unknownBody: You can’t open it right now. If you believe this is a mistake, write to support@motir.co.
suspended.switchFailed: That organization couldn’t be opened. Reload the page.

fleet.title: Fleet · running now
fleet.subtitle: What {org} is running on Motir’s fleet right now, and whether it is being charged for it.
fleet.subtitleEmpty: Nothing is running on the fleet for this organization.

facts.planCiUnreadable: Plan {plan} · hosted runs at once: {runs} · agents per person: {perUser} · agents running: {running} · CI limit unreadable
facts.planExemptOverride: Plan No plan limit · CI jobs at once: {ci} (override)

stop.explainer: Stopping ends this organization’s charged work now: CI, hosted agent runs and agent instances. It does not suspend the organization.
stop.notPermitted: Only a superadmin can stop an organization’s containers. You are signed in as {role}.

confirm.title: Stop {org}’s containers?
confirm.lead: This ends what {org} is running on Motir’s fleet right now:
confirm.ci: {runs, plural, one {CI run cancelled} other {CI runs cancelled}} and {containers} {containers, plural, one {CI container destroyed} other {CI containers destroyed}}
confirm.ciUnknown: CI runs not counted — GitHub could not be read; the stop still cancels them — and {containers} {containers, plural, one {CI container destroyed} other {CI containers destroyed}}
confirm.hosted: {count, plural, one {hosted agent run ended} other {hosted agent runs ended}}
confirm.instances: {count, plural, one {agent instance hibernated} other {agent instances hibernated}}
confirm.index: {count, plural, one {index container} other {index containers}} left to finish — indexing is Motir’s own cost and is never charged to the organization
confirm.notSuspension: This is not a suspension. Nothing is blocked: {org}’s next CI run, agent run or agent start goes through normal admission.
confirm.asOf: Counted at {time}. The stop acts on whatever is running when you confirm.
confirm.previewFailedBody: Nothing has been stopped. You confirm a stop against its counts, so try again.
confirm.reasonLabel: Reason — required, written to the audit log
confirm.reasonPlaceholder: Why are you stopping this organization’s containers?
confirm.reasonHint: Shown on this card and in the audit log. Say what you saw.
confirm.reasonRequired: Enter a reason. Nothing was stopped.

result.ci: {runs, plural, one {# CI run cancelled} other {# CI runs cancelled}} · {stopped, plural, one {# CI container destroyed} other {# CI containers destroyed}}
result.ciPartial: CI: {runs} runs cancelled · {stopped} of {total} containers destroyed
result.hosted: {ended, plural, one {# hosted agent run ended} other {# hosted agent runs ended}}
result.instances: {hibernated, plural, one {# agent instance hibernated} other {# agent instances hibernated}}
result.failed: {count} could not be stopped — the reconciler will retry.

error.notPermittedBody: Your platform role changed since this page loaded. Nothing was stopped.
error.notFoundBody: This organization no longer exists. Nothing was stopped.
error.failedBody: Some containers may have stopped before the error. The counts on this card have been read again — check them; a second stop acts only on what is still running.

last.title: Last stop
last.counts: {runs} CI runs · {containers} CI containers · {hosted} hosted runs · {instances} agent instances

modelLists.readOnly: Only a superadmin can change these lists.
modelLists.reasonLabel: Reason — required, written to the audit log
modelLists.reasonPlaceholder: Why are you changing the list?
modelLists.reasonHint: Shown to any operator reading this change later.

error.notPermitted: Only a superadmin can change this list.
error.failed: Something went wrong, and nothing was changed. Try again.
error.unavailable: motir-ai didn’t respond, so nothing was changed. Try again.

planningList.title: Models planning may use
planningList.subtitle: An audience can be set only to a listed model that motir-ai offers for planning right now. Each entry is checked on every read.

reason.not_servable: The gateway no longer serves this model.
reason.not_chat: Not a chat model, so it cannot plan.
reason.unrated: No planning rate is in force for it.

add.title: Add a model planning may use
add.body: Once added, a superadmin can set any audience to it while motir-ai offers it.
add.pickerFoot: Models the gateway serves that can plan (chat, with a planning rate) and are not on the list yet.
add.nothing: Every model that can plan is already listed.

remove.title: Remove {model} from the planning list?
remove.body: No audience is set to it, so no planning job changes. It can be added back later.
remove.inUse: Not removed: {audiences} plan on {model}. Move that audience to another model first.
remove.fallback: Not removed: {model} is the fallback every audience plans on when its own model is withdrawn, so it always stays listed.

planningList.added: {model} added. Any audience can be set to it now.

unavailable.title: Couldn’t load the planning-model list
unavailable.body: The planning service (motir-ai) didn’t respond, so no list is shown. Nothing has changed, and no value is guessed.

runModels.title: Hosted-run models
runModels.subtitle: Which models a hosted run may use, for every project. A project chooses from the listed models that motir-ai offers right now.
runModels.lineLive: A listed model that motir-ai stops offering disappears from every picker at once. An unlisted model never appears.
runModels.lineProjectsBody: They see its result: the Run hosted picker and their hosted-agent settings offer only these models.

card.title: Models a hosted run may use
card.subtitle: Seeded with every model motir-ai offered for hosted runs when the list was first read, so no project lost the model it had chosen.

runModels.notOffered: Not in motir-ai’s hosted-run offer right now: it is withdrawn, unrated, not a chat model, or its provider is not configured for hosted runs.

add.title: Add a model for hosted runs
add.body: Projects can choose it for Run hosted and their per-difficulty settings as soon as it is added.
add.pickerFoot: Models motir-ai offers for hosted runs that are not on the list yet.
add.nothing: Every model motir-ai offers for hosted runs is already listed.
add.notOffered: Not added: motir-ai no longer offers {model} for hosted runs.

remove.title: Remove {model} from hosted-run models?
remove.body: No project can choose it for a hosted run from now on. No project and no platform default uses it.
remove.inUse: Not removed: {model} is in use. {platformDefaultClause}{projectsClause} Change those first.

inUseParts.platformDefault: It is Motir’s platform default for {levels}.
inUseParts.projects: {n, plural, one {# project uses it} other {# projects use it}}: {list}.

remove.notListed: Not removed: {model} is no longer listed.

runModels.added: {model} added. Projects can choose it for hosted runs now.

empty.title: No model is listed
empty.body: No hosted run can start until a model is added. Add one from motir-ai’s offer.
empty.bodyReadOnly: No hosted run can start until a superadmin adds a model.

unavailable.title: Couldn’t load hosted-run models
unavailable.body: motir-ai didn’t respond, so whether each listed model is offered is unknown and no list is shown. Nothing has changed.

ideas.title: Ideas
ideas.subtitle: The ideas motir.co shows under Ideas to build, active and retired. Correct an idea, or retire it with a reason; the research skill adds new ones.
ideas.auditBody: Saving, retiring and deleting each write a row to the audit log with your name. motir.co picks a change up within the hour.

search.label: Search
search.placeholder: Search title, pitch, gap or tag

empty.title: No ideas yet
empty.body: Ideas are added in batches by the motir-ideas research skill, not on this page. Once a batch lands, every idea shows here for review.

error.title: Couldn’t load the ideas
error.body: Something went wrong reading the idea store, so none is shown. Nothing has changed.

ideas.readOnly: Read-only for support. Editing, retiring and deleting ideas is an operator’s or a superadmin’s job.

edit.title: Edit idea

tags.hint: Existing tags only · at most 6 · new tags come from the research skill

edit.motirOnly: Why Motir would buy it and Who else needs it belong to a Motir-would-buy idea only. Switch Kind to show them.
edit.unchanged: Nothing to save — change a field, or tick Mark as reviewed today.
edit.refused: Not saved — {n, plural, one {one field needs} other {# fields need}} fixing. Nothing was changed. The fields are marked below.
edit.saved: Saved. Your changes show here now and on motir.co within the hour.

fieldError.title: Give the idea a title of at most 120 characters.
fieldError.pitch: Write a pitch of at most 400 characters.
fieldError.motirOnly: Clear this on a direction, or switch Kind to Motir would buy.
fieldError.evidenceRequired: A direction needs at least one evidence row.
fieldError.url: Use a full link that starts with https://.
fieldError.sourceDate: Use a real date as YYYY-MM-DD, or leave it empty.
fieldError.capability: Write the line (at most 300), or remove it.
fieldError.unknownTag: {tag} is no longer a tag; remove it.

retire.title: Retire “{title}”?
retire.body: It leaves motir.co within the hour and moves under Retired here, with your reason. Nothing is deleted.
retire.reason: Reason — required, shown on the idea and written to the audit log
retire.placeholder: Why is this idea no longer worth building?
retire.already: Not retired — this idea was already retired. Someone retired it while you had the page open, so your reason was not recorded. The page now shows who retired it and why.
retire.done: Retired. It leaves motir.co within the hour.

delete.title: Delete “{title}” for good?
delete.body: Deleting removes the idea, its evidence and its tags and cannot be undone. Use it for an idea that was added by mistake; to take a real idea down, retire it instead. The audit log keeps the slug, the title and your reason.
delete.reason: Reason — required, written to the audit log
delete.placeholder: Why is this idea being deleted?
delete.done: Deleted “{title}”. It is gone from the store and from motir.co; the audit log keeps the record.

refused.notPermitted: Not done — your staff role does not allow this. Nothing was changed.
refused.notFound: This idea no longer exists. Someone deleted it while you had the page open.
refused.failed: Something went wrong, so nothing was changed. Try again.

fleetSettings.title: Fleet settings
fleetSettings.subtitle: Where a superadmin decides whose CI runs on Motir's own machines. Every change asks for a reason and is written to the audit log.
fleetSettings.empty: No project offers fleet CI — no meta-org project has a private repository in a connected org.

setting.title: Run Motir's private repositories' CI on the fleet
setting.explanation: When on, every CI job in Motir's private repositories on {org} requests the {label} label and runs on the shared {fleet} machines, attributed to moooon B.V. When off, they run on GitHub-hosted runners. No workflow file changes either way.

fleetSettings.blocked: Can't turn on until every condition is met.
fleetSettings.offNeverBlocked: Turning off never waits on readiness.

variable.present: {name} = {value} on {org} (private repositories) — new jobs request the fleet.
variable.absent: {name} is not set on {org} — jobs fall back to GitHub-hosted runners.
variable.unknown: Couldn't read {name} on {org} — GitHub answered HTTP {status}.
variable.unreachable: Couldn't read {name} on {org} — GitHub could not be reached.

onAbsent.title: Stored on, but GitHub disagrees.
onAbsent.body: {name} is not set on {org}, so new jobs still run on GitHub-hosted runners. Turn the setting off and on again to write it.

offPresent.title: Stored off, but GitHub disagrees.
offPresent.body: {name} is still set on {org}, so new jobs still request the fleet. Turn the setting on and off again to remove it.

repositories.count: {count, plural, one {# private repository} other {# private repositories}}, read at runtime from project {project}'s private repositories on {org}

fleetSettings.monitoringLine: Motir's machines appear under moooon B.V. in Monitoring › Fleet

onCallout.title: Motir's CI is on the fleet.

degraded.title: Not ready while on.
degraded.body: New jobs will queue until this is fixed or the setting is turned off.

readiness.title: Readiness
readiness.subtitle: Nine conditions, in the order a job meets them. A condition that couldn't be checked counts as not met.
readiness.notReady: Not ready — {count, plural, one {# condition} other {# conditions}} not met

why.kill_switch_engaged: The fleet kill switch is engaged ({variable}=0), so no fleet machine boots. An operator unsets or raises it.
why.app_not_installed: The motir-studio App is not installed on {org}. An owner of {org} installs it.
why.app_suspended: The motir-studio App on {org} has been suspended since {date}. An owner of {org} unsuspends it.
why.permission_missing: The motir-studio App on {org} holds {permission}: none, and needs write. An owner of {org} accepts the permission request.
why.permission_insufficient: The motir-studio App on {org} holds {permission}: {granted}, and needs write. An owner of {org} accepts the permission request.
why.not_subscribed: The App is not subscribed to workflow_job events, so GitHub never tells Motir a job is queued. Whoever administers the motir-studio App subscribes it in the App's settings.
why.repositories_not_granted: The App's installation on {org} does not reach {repositories}. An owner of {org} adds them to the installation's repository access.
why.no_private_repositories: Project {project} has no private repository in {org}, so there is nothing for the fleet to run.
why.not_attributable: A queued job from {repositories} would not be attributed to project {project}, so it would stay queued until GitHub expires it. Reconnect the repository to the project so its mirror row is current.
why.no_runner_group: Project {project} has no runner group in {org}. An operator runs {script} --project {project}.
why.sync_pending: The project's runner group in {org} is out of sync with its repositories. An operator runs {script} --project {project}.
why.jobs_not_runnable: {count, plural, one {# job} other {# jobs}} can't run on the fleet runner image yet. Whoever maintains the fleet image adds the missing tool; a job that needs another operating system stays unrunnable until it leaves the private set.
why.not_inventoried: {repositories} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} not in the fleet job inventory, so nobody has checked the runner image can run {count, plural, one {its} other {their}} jobs. Whoever maintains the inventory re-runs it.
why.inventory_stale: The workflows of {repositories} changed after the fleet job inventory measured them. Whoever maintains the inventory re-runs it.
why.read_failed: Couldn't check this: GitHub answered HTTP {status}. Counts as not met until a check succeeds.
why.read_unreachable: Couldn't check this: GitHub could not be reached. Counts as not met until a check succeeds.
why.read_failedNoStatus: Couldn't check this. Counts as not met until a check succeeds.
why.app_not_readable: Can't be checked until the motir-studio App is installed and readable on {org}.

jobs.scope: This covers the inventoried image built from main, not the image production boots.

confirm.onBody: Off → On. Every new CI job in {count, plural, one {# repository} other {# repositories}} will run on the fleet and be charged to moooon B.V.'s pool: {repositories}. Jobs already running finish where they started.
confirm.offBody: On → Off. New jobs go back to GitHub-hosted runners; jobs already running on the fleet finish there. Turning off never waits on readiness.
confirm.reasonLabel: Reason — required, written to the audit log
confirm.reasonPlaceholderOn: Why are you turning this on?
confirm.reasonPlaceholderOff: Why are you turning this off?
confirm.reasonHint: Shown to any operator reading this change later. “Testing” on its own answers nothing.
confirm.reasonHintEmpty: The button stays disabled until a reason is typed — the same rule the server applies.

refused.reasonMissing: Not turned {direction}: a reason is required, and it is written to the audit log with this change. Nothing changed.
refused.alreadyBody: Another superadmin changed it first, so nothing was written and no audit row was added.
refused.githubStatus: Not turned {direction}: GitHub refused to {operation} {name} on {org} (HTTP {status}).
refused.githubUnreachable: Not turned {direction}: GitHub could not be reached to {operation} {name} on {org}.
refused.nothingChanged: Nothing changed: the setting and the GitHub variable are as they were.
refused.notReady: Not turned on: the fleet stopped being ready after this page loaded.
refused.notReadyList: Not met now: {conditions}. Nothing changed. The readiness below has been checked again.
refused.notPermitted: Not changed: only a superadmin can change this setting.
refused.targetUnknown: Not changed: this project and organisation are no longer offered this setting. Reload the page.
refused.failed: Not turned {direction}: something went wrong. Reload the page to see the setting as it is now.

done.on: Turned on. New jobs request the fleet from now on.
done.off: Turned off. New jobs go back to GitHub-hosted runners.

unavailable.title: Couldn't load the fleet setting
unavailable.body: The setting or its readiness could not be read, so no state is shown and no switch is offered. This is a read error — nothing has changed, and no value is guessed.

legal.signUpNotice: By creating a Motir account you agree to our <terms>Terms of Service</terms> and <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.

reconsent.body: We won't treat carrying on in silence as agreement, so we're asking you to read what changed and say yes. Nothing has been deleted, your projects and workspaces are untouched, and your subscription has not changed.
reconsent.agreeFailed: We couldn't record that just now. Please try again.
reconsent.askAgain: We'll ask again the next time you sign in. Or <decline>tell us you don't accept</decline>.
reconsent.deferredBody: You've been signed out and nothing has changed. We'll ask again the next time you sign in, and you can read the new Terms whenever you like.
reconsent.declineHeadline: If you don't accept, you can close your account
reconsent.declineBody: Your Terms say that if you don't accept a material change you may end your agreement and get back the unused part of anything you've prepaid. That's still true — and nothing happens on this screen until you choose it.
reconsent.declineFoot: Would rather talk to a person about it? Write to <contact>legal@motir.co</contact> and we'll answer.

workItemTodos.emptyHint: Break this item's work into steps you can tick off, one operation each.

errors.forbidden: You do not have permission to change this item's steps.
errors.empty: A step needs to say what to do.
errors.textTooLong: A step is one operation, so it is capped at {limit} characters. Split it into two steps.
errors.commandTooLong: A command is capped at {limit} characters.
errors.notesTooLong: Instructions are capped at {limit} characters. A step needing more than that is a work item.
errors.reorderConflict: The list changed while you were moving that step. Reload and try again.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

myAgents.subtitle: Your own agents, on your own sign-in, in Motir’s cloud — {project}
myAgents.subtitleNarrow: Your own agents, on your own sign-in — {project}

Motir charges its machine time while it runs and its storage every day, and it sleeps when you stop using it.
myAgents.loadFailed: We couldn’t load your agents. Refresh to try again — nothing about them has changed.

progress.starting: Booting — cloning the project’s repositories into the home
progress.hibernating: Stopping the machine — your home stays
progress.waking: Starting a fresh machine on your home
progress.deleting: Destroying the machine and its home

myAgents.failedWayOut: Wake to try again, or delete it.

stop.credits: Stopped: your organization ran out of credits. Add credits, then wake it.
stop.backstop: Stopped after 12 hours running. Wake it to carry on.
stop.admin_stop: Stopped by Motir support. Wake it to carry on.

create.title: New agent
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: Only you see it. Letters, numbers and dashes.

mergeMode.title: Merging pull requests
mergeMode.desc: What happens when a pull request for this project’s work is ready to merge. A project whose repositories Motir hosts starts at Merge automatically; a project holding any repository of your own starts at Ask before merging.

manual.label: Ask before merging
manual.hint: When its checks pass, a person approves the pull request in Motir before it is merged. Nothing reaches your default branch without that yes.

auto.label: Merge automatically
auto.hint: When its checks pass, Motir merges the pull request without asking anyone. The record says this setting allowed it — not that a person approved it.
auto.blockedByReviewAgent: Turn the review agent off to merge automatically.

reviewAgent.title: Review agent
reviewAgent.desc: When a work item's pull requests pass their checks, a Motir agent reads the change against the item — its description, acceptance criteria and How to test — before you are asked to approve it. If it finds a problem, the item goes to To fix with the agent's findings, and nobody is asked to approve it.
reviewAgent.onWhat: Every work item is reviewed before you are asked to approve it.
reviewAgent.offWhat: A work item is offered for approval as soon as its checks pass.
reviewAgent.unavailableWhat: This project merges automatically, so nothing waits for a review. Choose Ask before merging to turn the review agent on.
reviewAgent.billingNote: Each review is a hosted agent run, paid from your organisation's AI credits.
reviewAgent.offNote: Turning this off cancels reviews in progress — those work items go straight to the ordinary flow.

designApproval.title: Design approval
designApproval.desc: A published design result waits for a person to approve it. The work built on the design cannot start until they do.
designApproval.onWhat: Every published design waits for a person to approve it.
designApproval.offWhat: Published designs are approved automatically, and each approval says this setting made it.
